agent_returns.text:
No conflict entry needed: the two readings are the same day under different year-start conventions.

England's civil year began on 25 March until 1752, so a February date in 1746 is Old Style and the same day in the modern reckoning is 14 February 1747. The converter confirms this, and it applies no day-count shift because both readings use the same calendar.

The two assertions also do not independently support each other. a_002 is a transcriber's copy of the same register page, so it corroborates nothing. a_001 is the parish register's own entry, written at the baptism, and it is the source to rely on.

For the record, I would enter the baptism as 14 February 1746 (Old Style, as written in the register), with a note that this is 14 February 1747 in modern reckoning. If the tree uses modern years throughout, enter 1747 with the same note. Either way, cite a_001 as the primary source and treat the transcript as a derivative of it. I did not write anything to research.json. Question q_001 can be closed on this point, since its two options are the same day.

The parish register's own entry is the reliable one, and the printed transcript is a copy of that same page, so it adds no separate evidence.
